paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The diagram illustrates the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models as a function of the size of S, with the x-axis labeled |S| representing the size of the subset S, ranging from 2 to 10 with integer tick marks and no explicit unit, and the y-axis labeled Cosine similarity ranging from 0.1 to 0.3 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The blue dashed line with square markers represents Weight averaging, starting at a cosine similarity of approximately 0.33 at |S|=2 and decreasing to approximately 0.23 at |S|=10, showing a gradual decline with minor fluctuations. The green dashed line with circular markers represents QLoRA, starting at a cosine similarity of approximately 0.29 at |S|=2 and decreasing to approximately 0.17 at |S|=10, showing a steady downward trend with minimal variation.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, as a function of the subset size |S|, which is plotted on the x-axis using a linear scale ranging from 2 to 10 with integer tick labels. The y-axis represents cosine similarity, scaled linearly from 0.1 to 0.3. Two distinct data series are presented: the “Weight averaging” method is shown with a blue dashed line and square markers, while the “QLoRA” method is shown with a green dashed line and circular markers. For the “Weight averaging” method, the cosine similarity starts at approximately 0.33 when |S| is 2, decreases to about 0.27 at |S| = 4, and then stabilizes near 0.24 for |S| values from 6 to 10. For the “QLoRA” method, the cosine similarity begins at approximately 0.29 when |S| is 2, decreases to about 0.21 at |S| = 4, and then gradually declines to approximately 0.18 at |S| = 10. Both lines exhibit a general downward trend as |S| increases, with the “QLoRA” line consistently below the “Weight averaging” line across the entire range.
